Q: How to use my custom yaml tag in Ansible? A:

As @Marko Kohtala said, Ansible uses its own loader which inherits yaml.SafeConstructor and the custom YAML tag constructor must be added before a YAML input file is parsed.

As of Ansible 13.1 (core 2.20.1), inventory plugins appear to be loaded after reading the configuration file but before any other YAML files. Here is an example of a dummy inventory plugin, that does nothing to the inventory, but adds a constructor for a tag that will translate english to pig-latin:

playbooks/inventory_plugins/to_pig.py

import re
from ansible._internal._yaml._loader import AnsibleLoader
from ansible.plugins.inventory       import BaseInventoryPlugin

class InventoryModule(BaseInventoryPlugin):
  pass

def to_pig_constructor(self, node) -> str:
  def doword(word):
    cons,front = re.match(r'(?i)^([^aeiou]*)(.*)$', word).groups()
    back       = cons+"ay" if cons else "way"
    return front+back
  return " ".join([doword(word) for word in node.value.split()])

AnsibleLoader.add_constructor('!to-pig',  to_pig_constructor)

playbooks/playbook.yml

---
- hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: no
  vars:
    mypig: !to-pig "take me to your leader"

  tasks:
    - name: pig-test
      debug:
        var: mypig

ansible.cfg was modified to enable the inventory plugin:

[inventory]
enable_plugins = host_list, script, auto, yaml, ini, toml, to_pig

ansible-playbook playbooks/playbook.yml

PLAY [localhost] **************************************************************************************

TASK [pig-test] **************************************************************************************
ok: [localhost] => {
    "mypig": "aketay emay otay ouryay eaderlay"
}

PLAY RECAP **************************************************************************************
localhost                  : ok=1    changed=0    unreachable=0    failed=0    skipped=0    rescued=0    ignored=0

This monkey-patch works but the Ansible guys don't like it. So the solution may not be stable.

Some notes about Inventory Plugins:

  • For a local plugin to be available to all playbooks and roles, it must be added to one of the default locations or it's location must be given in the configuration file or environment variables.

  • For a local plugin to be available only to a given playbook or role, as in this example, it must be added to the inventory_plugins subfolder of the role or playbook folder.

  • If part of a collection, the plugin must reside in the collection's plugins/inventory directory and the config file must use the fully-qualified collection name (FQCN) to enable it. For example, if this plugin was part of the amazing.stuff collection, the config file would need to include:

    [inventory]
enable_plugins = host_list, script, auto, yaml, ini, amazing.stuff.to_pig

  • As an alternative to modifying the enable_plugins setting in the configuration file, an inventory plugin can be specified in a YAML inventory config file.

    For example, if the config file inventory setting identifies a directory, rather than a file, that directory may include a config file for the inventory plugin:

    inventory/to_pig.yml

    plugin: to_pig

    The auto inventory plugin will then load the to_pig.py plugin, automatically, if it's found in the appropriate directory.

    If the plugin is part of a collection, the full FQCN must be given.

Q: Database connection failing as soon as the parent ssh shell is terminated, even though I backgrounded and disowned A:

I believe this is happening because you're executing ssh with its -t option. This sets up a controlling TTY, which acts on the process group. If you must use -t, then your background process probably needs to use setsid() to escape whatever effect results from closing the controlling TTY. I'm surprised your background process continues to run at all; when I played around with this on Linux, my background process terminated.

Q: Launch suprocesses in Python by chunks and wait until end for start the next chunk A:

We execute this chunks times:

    [p.wait() for p in procs]

Inevitably there will be one of the ten workers that finishes first, and another that finishes last. In many, many practical situations there is an "interesting" amount of variation between those elapsed times. We call that the Straggler Effect.

Your code should be doing wait4() in parallel across the ten workers, and immediately forking off a new worker when one exits (not when ten exit).

The usual idiom for that is to use a multiprocessing pool, but you did not import that standard library so I have to assume you have good reasons. The next best thing would be to let make worry about those details. Create a Makefile:

OUT = \
 task00.txt \
   ...
 task99.txt \

all: $(OUT)

%.txt:
        python mpirun options
        touch $@

Then make -j10 executes what you want, staying within the memory budget.

That touch is arguably an ugly wart. Perhaps the mpirun child produces a result file that make can see? Or perhaps GNU parallel is a better fit for your use case.

it = 10

nit: That's not a terrific identifier. Commonly we use it to describe an iterator or an iterable.

Q: Batch script to zip a folder using InfoZip A:

Here is the documentation for info-zip:

https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/resolute/en/man1/zip.1.html#examples

In contrary to what zip.exe shows, the syntax for zipping files is this:

zip -r zipfilename zipfilecontents

Example:

zip -r myzip.zip c:\myfolder\*.*

The -r parameter includes subfolders as well.

Problem is that the complete folder structure is included in the zip. I have not found a solution for this yet.
